newsitem.title: USA: Avon president's departure seen not disruptive.
newsitem.headline: Avon president's departure seen not disruptive.

text.p: Avon Products Inc Chairman James Preston's decision to stay on another two years cost the company its president on Tuesday, but one analyst said Edward Robinson's departure would not be disruptive because Avon has a deep management team.
Avon shares closed up 2-1/8 to 63-3/8, not far below their year high of 63-7/8.
"It's surprising, but not disruptive," J.P. Morgan analyst Michael Grant said of the decision by Robinson, Avon's president and chief operating officer, to step down.
"They've got a deep management team," Grant said.
Avon in a news release said that Robinson, 57, left because he disagreed with the decision by Preston, 64, to stay on as chairman and chief executive.
"You can infer that he obviously wanted that No. 1 position," Grant said. "I would assume that, basically, he was hoping the management progression would include him as chairman and CEO."
Avon spokesman Vic Beaudet said Preston would take on Robinson's duties, including the title of president.
Preston in the news release said he would stay on "at least" for the next two years and a top priority would be ensuring a smooth transition in senior management before he retires.
Grant speculated that Christina Gold and Andrea Jung, two Avon executive vice presidents, might be considered possible future chief executives. Beaudet said no succession has been established.
Grant said Avon under Preston in the last few years "has done a very good job of turning itself around."
Avon is a direct seller of beauty products and related goods. Among its brands are Anew, Skin-So-Soft and Avon Color.
